description.p: Drift is a free desktop video editor that feels simple from the first cut. Drop in video, photos, and music, add effects and stickers, generate captions automatically, and export — no subscription, no watermark, and no account required.
Great for social videos, explainers, and everyday projects. Cut subjects out of a frame, animate to the beat, style text and shapes, then add fonts and stickers only when you need them.
What you get:

ul.li: Multi-track timeline — trim, split, snap, and undo as you go
Effects, transitions, and reusable look templates
Stickers, emoji, titles, and shapes for a finished look
Auto captions from speech in your video
Cut out subjects, mask clips, and key out green screens
Speed changes, reverse playback, and fades
Animate to the beat of your music
Mix audio and clean up background noise
Optional addons for fonts, stickers, and extras
Project bundles that keep your media together

screenshot.caption: The editor with the media bin, preview, inspector and timeline
Grading in the Color workspace with looks and scopes
Shaping motion in the keyframe curve editor
Masking and tracking part of a shot
Editing styled captions generated from speech
Mixing music with audio effects and meters
Lighting a 3D model on the timeline
Styling a title with built-in text packs

description.p: Drift 0.9.1 is a bug fix update for the interface, with updates to the 3D workspace as well.

ul.li: 3D workspace: two live views side by side, After Effects-style coordinates and a reworked camera
Undo history is saved in the project file, with no 50-step limit, and projects save in the background
Shape crops: crop a clip to a circle, polygon, star or heart and pan and zoom the content inside it
The Crop window opens on the frame under the playhead and can rotate and flip
New Privacy Blur effect with blur, mosaic and solid bar modes, and a new Reverb audio effect
Remove silence and Sync by audio clip actions

Timeline: replace a clip's media with another library asset, a Move to track menu, remove all empty tracks, dissolve a composite clip back into its clips, and tabs to switch between composite sequences
Moving a linked video to another track takes its audio with it
A shared curve picker for animations, with custom curves
A miter limit for text and shape strokes
Choose where Drift keeps its cache
Text, shapes and Lottie clips render sharply at their on-screen size, including fractional text sizes
Relinking a missing file updates every clip that uses it and offers to relink files next to it

Timeline fixes: clips can be split and trimmed down to one frame, the playhead no longer steps backwards during playback, dropped transitions are added as chosen, fade handles drag again and follow in/out animations, clips shrink with zoom, and track and keyframe headers resize

Interface fixes: context menus stay on screen and scroll when tall, transform grips work outside the canvas, the scale link toggle works again, number fields no longer change on hover, empty panels and toasts draw inside their bounds, and the library tab rail can be resized
Render fixes: exports above the project size render at the output resolution, transition edges no longer show dark fringes, and star masks draw five points
Android: more reliable clip drag and trim handles on the timeline
Translations: Japanese, Portuguese (Portugal) and Vietnamese updated

description.p: Drift 0.9 lets you shape the editor around the job: workspaces with your own layouts, themes, a colour grading workspace and a much better keyframe editor.

ul.li: Workspaces: design your own layouts, open panels in extra windows and switch between preset views for editing, colour, keyframes, subtitles, masking and tracking, and Source Lab
Themes: dark and light plus the translucent Graphite and Frost themes, window backdrops, and importing your own themes
Colour grading: a Color workspace with a Color Grade effect, colour wheels, curves, hue curves and per-colour HSL, looks with .cube LUT import, and histogram, waveform and vectorscope readings

Keyframe editor: a Keyframes workspace with a property tree, lanes and a curve editor; multi-key selection, copy and paste, stretching and scaling keys; per-segment easing presets including elastic and bounce, saved easings and optional bezier handles

Source Lab replaces Cut / Trim: a frame-accurate source viewer with JKL and timecode entry, favourite and reject ranges, markers and scene splits, plus crop, speed, loudness, denoise, stabilize and upscale, with replace in bin, add as copy or export to a file
Masking and Tracking workspace: brush and polygon masks, point and planar tracking, AI object masks, Blur this area, per-frame brush fixes on AI cutouts and locking a tracked object to the screen
Subtitles workspace with a cue grid, lane, text and timing panels and VTT support
Quick Setup on first run: language, theme, interface size, essential addons and tips
Extras store and marketplace in their own windows, with an install queue, automatic dependencies and every download tracked in one place
Search everything with Ctrl+K, including panels, settings and controls
A redesigned settings dialog with search, a network proxy, an interface graphics API choice and import and export of preferences
Select several clips in the preview and transform them together, in 2D and 3D
Timeline: sub-clips from a source's in/out range, automatic crossfades on overlaps, trim to playhead buttons, auto-select under the playhead, alignment guides and waveforms scaled by clip volume
Inspector: drag numeric fields to scrub them, pick the scale origin from an anchor grid, and straighten crops
Effects: audio spectrum and waveform visualizers, text case and strikethrough, and miter, round and bevel stroke joins
AMD GPUs can run AI features through MIGraphX, and Drift offers another engine when the chosen one fails
Faster playback: background decoding pauses during playback, a 1/8 preview quality, and panels that load only when shown
New builds for Intel macOS, Windows on ARM and Linux on ARM
Android: a redesigned phone interface with a tabbed home and full-page tools, touch mask editing, and headphones used for playback
MCP: themes, crop and rotation, media bin folders, the marketplace, audio analysis and running several Drift instances at once

Fixes: changing a clip's speed keeps its source range, playback stays in sync after the audio device changes, large blurs stay smooth, edited media is kept on save, and Android imports files with unusual names
Translations: Chinese (Simplified) and Portuguese (Portugal) completed; Japanese, Polish, Russian, Spanish (Colombia), Tagalog and Vietnamese updated

Drift goes 3D: a 3D preview mode with a scene camera, Gaussian splats and lights you can place in the view. It also brings local text-to-speech with voice cloning, PDF clips, audio effects built from pedals, an Outline effect, a rebuilt text engine and a much more usable Android app.

ul.li: 3D preview mode: a free 3D view with a camera gizmo, orbit and zoom controls and a Blender-style fly mode; 3D models sit in the scene as world-space layers
Scene camera: add a camera track and pan, orbit and dolly every clip through it, with per-clip depth occlusion
Gaussian splats: import SOG, streamed SOG and 3DGS PLY files
3D lighting: four point and spot lights editable in the 3D view, and depth-effect clips shown as a relief with draggable light gizmos
Text to speech: generate speech and clone voices locally, with a voice library and voiceovers from subtitles
PDF clips: place PDF pages on the timeline and scroll through them

Audio effects made of pedals: filters, drive, reverb, convolution reverb, delay and more in series, parallel or frequency splits, with LFOs, envelope followers and step sequencers, and keyframable parameters
Outline effect: strokes, dashes, gradient fills, shadows, glows and torn, burnt, stamp and other edge styles around any clip
Text: edit text directly on the preview, system fonts and your own font files in the picker, colour emoji fonts, and new plain and bold styles
Link unrelated clips so they move and trim together
Import numbered image sequences as a single video clip
Proxies are kept next to the source footage and relinked automatically
Generated captions stay in sync when the clip's speed or direction changes
Close Gap can move a track's first clip to the start, and deleting with ripple on closes the gap
Projects open in the background behind a progress dialog
Notifications show one at a time, with a history under a bell in the header
Updates download only when you ask, are verified, and install in place on Windows, macOS and AppImage
macOS: an appearance-aware app icon and better native menu integration
MCP: tools for text to speech, PDFs, the 3D view, the scene camera, effect presets and closing projects

Fixes: undo for keyframe tangents, holds and bookmarks, panels no longer shrink on every launch, export reports why it failed, a project name is asked for on first save, AVI, MKV and WebM play in the macOS trim window, and fonts on Windows
Translations: Bengali added; Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Vietnamese and many others updated

description.p: Thanks to @rangaNP for the macOS icon, menu and update work; to André Mota for linking clips; to Jose Miguel Navarro for Close Gap and the MCP project tools; to @NipunSGeeTH for linked keyframe coordinates; to Mehedi Hasan for Bengali; to Paweł Korobajło for Polish; to @coolvitto for Japanese; and to Nguyễn Lam for Vietnamese.

A bug-fix release that stops the crashes on Intel graphics when scrubbing hardware-decoded video. It also brings a Face Retouch effect, AI video upscaling, speed control for composite clips and a batch of smaller fixes and additions.

ul.li: Fixed crashes in the Intel media driver (iHD) when scrubbing hardware-decoded video in the preview
Face Retouch: a beauty effect for smoothing skin, reshaping and lip and skin tone colour, with a numbered face picker and support for still images
Enhance video: upscale clips with a choice of models, with trim and crop before upscaling and a live frame preview
Speed adjustment for composite clips
Animated GIFs import as video and play on the timeline
Stabilized clips are rendered into the media bin as their own assets
Save media bin assets back out as files
Eye toggle to hide adjustment tracks, and nested adjustment lanes

Custom effects: new parameter types (2D points, choice lists, whole numbers and colours with alpha), keyframable colours and toggles, a My Effects filter and audio effects in .driftfx packages, which can now be imported directly
Install add-ons from .driftpkg or .zip files and from a custom add-ons folder
Market: a Sound Effects tab, asset variations and back buttons that stay in place while scrolling
MCP: agents can create, update, delete and export custom effects, transitions and audio effects
macOS: a native system menu bar, and install through Homebrew
Available on the Microsoft Store and Google Play

Fixes: effects work on people cutouts, ripple on edge trims, zoom-aware snapping, sized SVGs scale to the clip and keep their CSS styles, the market catalog reloads when its tab opens, package textures are no longer flipped, proxies no longer fill up the temp folder, and image export on Android
Translations: Korean, Polish and Portuguese (Portugal) added; Japanese and Vietnamese updated

description.p: Thanks to @rangaNP for the macOS menu bar and the Homebrew cask; to @mildannerofc for Korean and Portuguese (Portugal); to Paweł Korobajło for Polish; to @coolvitto for Japanese; and to @tojidotakarin for Vietnamese.

Huge performance improvements across the timeline, preview and playback, with the UI lag gone. Import 3D objects, light scenes with Studio Relight and depth effects, and tilt clips with 3D transforms. A redesigned audio mixer, recording straight onto the timeline, and proxy editing for heavy footage round out the release.

ul.li: Transcript-first editing: word-level transcripts with speaker detection, cut by deleting words, remove silences, and audio transitions
Composite clips: nest clips into a single clip you can move, trim and reuse
Transform layers: move, scale, rotate, tilt and fade several tracks as one (Ctrl+G), with a bracket in the track headers showing what the layer covers
3D clip transforms with tilt, depth and perspective, and a move, rotate and scale gizmo in global or local space
Import 3D models (.glb) as clips, and face props for the face effects
Depth effects: 3D relight, depth of field, fog and occlusion driven by estimated video depth, and Behind Subject for placing graphics behind people
Voiceover recording from the microphone onto a track, with live waveforms, gain, mic selection and pause
Redesigned audio mixer: resizable docked panel with per-track and master strips, pan knobs, stereo meters and a pinned master
Proxy editing, and a Convert to CFR option for variable frame rate phone footage
Non-destructive source framing to crop and reframe a video inside its clip
Videos with an alpha channel keep their transparency
Custom preview guides: build guide sets, drag guides on the preview and snap to them
Subtitles: generate for a selection of clips, merge subtitles, and a smoother editing workflow
A start screen for opening or starting a project, a full-project overview strip above the timeline, a transform scale slider, and dropping media straight from the file manager onto the timeline
A themed colour picker with an in-window eyedropper, and the chroma key colour picked from the Effects card
Market: Drift Assets as the home page, a stock browser across all sources, detail panels that slide over, and a remembered download folder
Performance: a GPU-drawn timeline, lighter trims and drags, lower memory use, smoother transitions during playback and hardware decoding for every clip once it is proven to work
Android: faster timeline scrubbing, touch-first clip gestures, drag and drop for every asset, in-process stabilization, and safer names for imported files
Audio fixes: the Limiter limits instead of adding gain, loudness and true peak are measured to the standard so Normalise no longer clips, and ducking keeps the music's own volume

Fixes: splitting keeps effects and animation on both halves, imported media is centred on the canvas, pinned effects stay on their own clip during transitions, the Duotone effect renders again, the preview no longer flashes on slow GPUs, and arrow keys jog the playhead on Wayland
Nightly builds, AppImage update information, a warning for unsupported graphics drivers, and an Agent access option that starts on launch with a persistent token
Translations: Arabic and Colombian Spanish added; Japanese, Spanish, Vietnamese, French (Canada) and Sinhala updated

description.p: Thanks to @jmn8718 for the start screen, the timeline overview strip, source framing, the Agent start-on-launch option and decoder and addon install fixes; to @gelvezz23 for the chroma key tab and Colombian Spanish; to @dratiux for Arabic; to @coolvitto for Japanese; to @tojidotakarin for Vietnamese; to @CathodeAnode for French (Canada); and to Loposmo for Spanish.

Text and shapes are redrawn through Skia with layered styles, gradients and a new animation engine, Lottie and SVG clips arrive on the timeline, over a hundred new transitions land in the add-ons catalog, and Windows gets a Direct3D zero-copy path with fixes for NVIDIA stutter.

ul.li: Text styles: fill, stroke, shadow, glow and extrude layers with solid, gradient, texture or shader paints, a Looks gallery (Neon, Chrome, Holographic, Glitch, Outline, Echo and more), curved baselines and keyframable size, tracking and layer settings

Text animations: per-character, word or line animators with In, Out and Loop preset galleries — typewriter, type-on blur, rise by word, snap together, glitch, flicker, colour wave, wipe, karaoke pop and bounce, and 40 more
Shapes share the same style stack: gradient fills, multiple strokes, shadows, glows and dashes, all keyframable so shapes can animate
Lottie (.lottie, .json) and SVG files import as vector clips, with a Motion inspector for editing slots, playback options and poster frames
100+ new GPU transitions ported from gl-transitions, available through the add-ons catalog, plus easing curves for every transition
In-app Marketplace for browsing and downloading stock media, with a separate download-queue window
Adjustment layers in the Effects tab; masks are now keyframeable adjustment layers with on-canvas handles and their own Masks tab
Cutouts via Robust Video Matting, and Paste Attributes with selective picking across multi-clip selections

Windows: Direct3D 11 zero-copy decoding and a GPU switcher for hybrid laptops; fixed CUDA zero-copy and CUDA/OpenGL interop stutter on NVIDIA, hybrid-GPU decode, display-cadence stutter and the black preview on software OpenGL; new playback diagnostics and a warning for hardware-acceleration settings that will not work on the current machine
Audio: multi-channel waveform view, decibel volume control, multi-track audio extraction, and separate-audio / unlink actions on the timeline

Media bin: tree view, Import Folder, nested folder moves, multi-select with Shift-click ranges and bulk actions, safe removal of in-use media, lossless 90° rotation correction and non-destructive trimming from the bin
Android: hardware-accelerated video decoding and a reworked mobile layout
Save As, track renaming, select-all-and-move, keyboard delete, Shift+Arrow frame-by-frame scrubbing, native shortcut labels on macOS, and settings moved into a dialog
MCP: headless CLI mode, text, shape and motion-graphics tools, and lower token usage
Translations: Tagalog and Vietnamese added; Japanese and Spanish updated

description.p: Thanks to @jmn8718 for lossless rotation correction, Import Folder, track renaming and the media bin multi-select and folder moves; to @gorio for safe media removal, keyboard delete, separate-audio and unlink actions, track numbering and native macOS shortcuts; to @TSFBCE24RhythmHeaveners for the Tagalog translation; to @tojidotakarin for Vietnamese; to @coolvitto for Japanese; and to @angelreyesvelazquezjesus-gif for Spanish.
A quick bug-fix release for NVIDIA users. If playback looks fine on your machine, you can skip this update.

ul.li: Fixed black flicker between frames during NVIDIA hardware-decoded preview.

description.p: This is the first public release of Drift for Android. On the desktop, preview and export stay on the GPU, the media bin gets folders, and Face Swap, video stabilization, and several new languages land in this version.

ul.li: First public Android app — edit on a phone with a touch UI, including crop and trim from the bin, and AV1 playback
Preview stays on the GPU instead of copying every frame through the CPU, so Full / Half / Quarter match the preview panel size
Export converts frames to the encoder format on the GPU; typical 8-bit exports are faster
Folders in the media bin: create, rename, nest, and move clips between them
Preview, trim, and crop a clip from the bin before putting it on the timeline
Face Swap effect: replace a face in a clip with a still photo
Video stabilization to smooth camera shake, with a smoothness slider and optional tripod lock
Settings → Interface scale (100–200%), and a first-launch language chooser
Timeline scroll pans left and right, Shift+scroll moves between tracks, and middle-click drag also pans
Closing a project with unsaved changes now asks Save / Don't Save / Cancel
Translations: Brazilian Portuguese, Chinese (Simplified), French (Canada), Spanish, Italian, and Sinhala

description.p: Thanks to @CathodeAnode for the French (Canada) translation, SVG icons, translatable UI strings, and restoring a maximized window after fullscreen on KDE; to @yosenstar for Chinese (Simplified); to @alexbassani for Brazilian Portuguese; to @roger-fernandes-Dev for timeline scroll and pan; and to @jmn8718 for folders in the media bin.
GPU decoding and encoding on every platform, effect and text presets you can reuse across projects, and a fix for NVIDIA on Wayland.

ul.li: Fixed the black preview on NVIDIA under Wayland — Drift now runs as a native Wayland app instead of falling back to X11
Video decoding for the preview now uses the GPU on Windows and macOS too, not only Linux, and you can pick the backend from the preview toolbar
Export can encode on the GPU with NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF, VAAPI or VideoToolbox
Copy an effect or a whole effect stack between clips, and save your own presets
Save the look of a title as a text style and reuse or share it
The subtitle editor follows the playhead, and titles can contain colour emoji
Save a project as readable JSON and open one back again
Close a gap on a track, or split just one clip instead of every clip under the playhead
Window size and panel proportions are remembered between sessions
A bug button in the header collects the details needed for a good bug report
Large media imports are faster and use far less memory

description.p: Thanks to @CathodeAnode for the NVIDIA Wayland fix and the media-library performance work, and to @jmn8718 for close gap and per-clip split.
A big update with macOS support, AI agent control, new editing tools, and a batch of everyday fixes.

ul.li: Added MCP support — you can now let AI agents like Claude Code control the editor
Improved macOS support, including a working video preview
.drift project files now open with the editor when you double-click them
Cut a multi-camera shoot by watching every camera at once and switching between them
Find scenes inside a clip and jump straight to them
New 3D Face Mesh effect that follows the face through the clip
Mark an In and Out on the timeline to play and export just that range
Export short clips as animated GIFs
A portrait layout for vertical videos, with the preview on top
Zoom and pan the preview; drag or delete keyframes on the graph
Choose 1440p when setting up a project
Windows releases include a portable zip that needs no installer
Pick a language in Settings — More languages coming soon
Choose how many words go in each auto-generated caption
Fixed lag and audio going out of sync when two clips from the same file overlap
Fixed silent playback on some Windows audio devices
Phone videos keep their portrait size instead of becoming a square
Transitions no longer reset when you click them
Scrolling over a slider no longer also scrolls the panel behind it
Starting a new project now fully clears the previous one

description.p: A quick bug-fix release for AppImage users only. If you installed Drift from Flathub, the Arch package or the Windows installer, nothing changes for you and there is no need to update.

ul.li: Videos that the AppImage refused to open, or played as a black picture, now work. The AppImage was bundling a cut-down copy of FFmpeg that didn't have several codecs.
The AppImage now runs natively on Wayland instead of falling back to XWayland. The Wayland platform plugin was missing from the bundle.

description.p: A polish release focused on export options, playback controls, and everyday editing quality-of-life.

ul.li: Export at different frame rates, including audio-only export
Export freeze frames as images; remember last export folder and settings
Playback controls for navigating the timeline
Animation tab with custom editable fade curves
Persist dark mode and media view; option to reopen the last project at startup
Timeline zoom stays centered on the playhead or cursor
Close gaps when trimming; clearer trim start/end icons
Avoid color-space conversion during composition that could reduce quality

description.p: A feature release with new editing tools, timeline and asset-browser improvements, UI polish, performance work, and a batch of bug fixes.

ul.li: Aspect-locked clip resize in the preview (hold Shift to stretch freely)
Type exact values into property sliders; drag from the slider head works reliably
Delete, rename, search, favorites, and category browsing in the asset panel
Replace media in place while keeping timeline clips, effects, and layout
Disable and reorder effects on a clip; beauty and makeup face effects
Audio tempo follows clip speed; reverse video builds a reverse proxy with progress
Freeze frame captures the full composited image; clearer timeline bookmarks
Fit timeline in view, wider zoom for long projects, and scrolling on smaller screens
Redesigned text properties panel and style packs in the Text assets tab
Prompt to install essential addons on startup; less intrusive update notifications
Reliable media drag-and-drop onto the timeline on Mutter / GNOME
Fixed file-picker extensions on Flatpak, subtitle cue waveforms, and the project setup dialog
Faster filmstrip thumbnails and lighter subtitle voice waveform mixing

description.p: Fixes for saving and exporting through the desktop file picker.

ul.li: Saving a project or exporting without typing a file extension no longer leaves the result as a hidden file in flatpak builds

description.p: A small fix-up release on top of the first public version.

ul.li: Curves in the keyframe editor are drawn sharply instead of blurred

description.p: The first public release of Drift — a free, open-source desktop video editor with no subscription, no watermark and no account.

ul.li: Multi-track timeline with trim, split, snap, ripple and full undo
GPU effects, transitions and reusable look templates
Titles, shapes, stickers and emoji
Automatic captions from the speech in your video
Subject cutout, clip masks and green-screen keying
Speed changes, reverse, fades and beat-synced animation
Audio mixing, an effect chain and background noise removal
Project bundles that keep a project and its media together
Export to MP4 (H.264 + AAC) that matches the preview
Optional addons for fonts, stickers, speech models and acceleration runtimes
